# aibris v0.15.2

This patch release makes guided review count work that continues in an
existing Codex session, not only sessions that start after review. It contains
only fixes to existing behavior.

## Highlights

- **Resumed and long-running sessions count as activity** (#636).
  - Codex appends to the same session file when a session is resumed or keeps
    running. aibris used only the time the session started, so work continued
    in an old session did not count as session activity. (A dirty worktree or
    a new commit could still lock it.)
  - A session's activity time is now the later of its start time and the
    session file's last modification. Guided review uses it for the 6-hour
    `recent_activity` lock, the 3-day minimum idle age, and the order in which
    the most recent worktrees per repository are kept.
  - Before removal, aibris compares this time with the reviewed value before
    the member loop, before each member, and before the owner directory. A
    later value stops the removal and records `activity_evidence_changed`,
    even when the new time is outside the 6-hour window. If an earlier member
    was already removed, the receipt is `partial` and the remaining members
    and the owner are kept.
  - Session files are stat'ed directly while the stores are walked, so on
    Windows an open session file does not report a stale size or write time.
    Files whose path, size, and modification time are unchanged are still not
    read again.
- **A Codex home that is a Windows junction fails closed** (#634, #636). When
  a Codex home (`~/.codex`, `CODEX_HOME`, an `AIBRIS_CODEX_HOMES` entry, or
  Orca's) is a junction or another reparse point, sessions recorded with the
  target path could fail to match their worktree. Such a home is now
  unavailable evidence at refresh and lookup, for native worktrees and for
  Orca aggregation, so active worktrees stay protected in guided review.

## Compatibility impact

- [x] **No public contract change.** No flag, JSON field, or reason code was
  added, removed, or renamed, and `schema_version` stays `1`.

## Upgrade and migration

No flag migration is required.

```bash
brew upgrade aibris
# or (Unix):
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sungjunlee/aibris/refs/heads/main/install.sh | bash -s -- v0.15.2
# or (Windows PowerShell):
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sungjunlee/aibris/refs/heads/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

- The Codex activity cache changed revision. An older cache is discarded and
  rebuilt the next time it is read.
- A worktree whose only session file was modified in the last 6 hours is now
  protected with `recent_activity` in guided review, even if the session
  started long ago. An older modification can still change which worktrees
  count as the most recent per repository and whether a worktree is younger
  than the minimum idle age.

## Safety

- Every earlier safeguard is unchanged: the single deletion gate, dry-run and
  confirmation, `--risky`, active-worktree protection, agent-state proof and
  grace, re-verification at the mutation boundary, and overlap safety.
- Where a Codex home still supplies session evidence, activity time is never
  earlier than in v0.15.1, so no `recent_activity` lock is lost. A junction
  home stops supplying evidence; its worktrees stay locked with
  `activity_evidence_unavailable` instead.
- Known limitations, tracked for follow-up:
  - Activity evidence is not recovered through a relocated session store
    (#634). On Windows, a junction in a parent directory of the Codex home is
    not yet detected (#634).
  - An append that lands after aibris's last check and before the removal
    itself cannot be seen.

## Windows status

Native Windows CI also runs the junction Codex home test (#636), in addition
to the coverage listed for v0.15.1: restored cleaner command tests, cache-leaf
and `sessions/` junction tests, the full `internal/safedelete`,
`internal/pathidentity`, and `internal/testutil` packages, and the production
PowerShell installer tests. Real vendor agent worktree layouts on Windows,
end-to-end delete mutation, and native arm64 execution remain experimental
and unmeasured. See `docs/WINDOWS.md`.
